title: Trade-group fan-out & rate-limit governor
body:
## Context
R3 closes the execution loop on Bybit demo. E27 supplies accounts and the key vault, E28 the per-account profiles and the trade-group definition, E29 the OMS and its order state machine, E32 brackets and the native-SL invariant, E39 the risk caps and kill-switch. **E34 is the multi-account execution primitive that sits on top of all of them**: one intent → N per-account legs, each sized and protected by *that account's own* profile, submitted in parallel against *N independent per-UID rate-limit budgets*, and tracked as one logical trade.

This is owner decision #5 (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Locked decisions — "one ticket → fan-out to N accounts as a trade group"); the normative design lives in `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0008-trade-group-fanout.md`, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §4.3 and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §9.

Two properties make this epic uniquely dangerous and drive its whole shape:
1. **Bybit rate limits are per-UID, shared across keys.** N accounts genuinely have N budgets, but the per-IP budget (600 req/5 s) is shared. A fan-out that discovers exhaustion mid-loop leaves a group half-placed with undefined semantics, so admission control must precede placement (`20-architecture.md` §4.3).
2. **Partial failure is normal, not exceptional.** A fan-out where some legs fill and some fail must raise a P0-visible reconciliation state with a one-click unwind of the successful legs — never a silent half-executed trade group (roadmap §7.2 E34 row).

Every leg carries a native exchange-side stop-loss (architecture principle P4, `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.8). This epic contains no code path that can open a leg without one.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories**
- **US-PROF-006** Fan-out an order to a trade group (Must) — the epic's core.
- **US-PROF-007** Trade-group lifecycle view (Must) — aggregate view, group actions, divergence detection.
- **US-PROF-008** Per-trade profile overrides (Should) — per-leg overrides inside the fan-out ticket (the profile schema itself is E28).
- **US-ORD-013** Mandatory native stop-loss (Must) — the fan-out path's share of the invariant; the enforcement engine is E32/M17, this epic proves no leg escapes it.
- **US-ORD-010** Flatten and cancel-all (Must) — the *group* variants ("flatten group", "close group 50%"); the single-account variant is E31.
- **US-ORD-014** Pre-trade risk preview (Should) — the *group* aggregation of the preview; the single-account preview is E30.

US-PROF-001..005 (profile schema, sizing rules, allowed symbols, server-side risk caps, group definition) belong to **E28** and are consumed here, never re-implemented.

**Screens:** SCR-061 Trade-group ticket (multi-account fan-out), SCR-062 Trade-group manager, SCR-063 Positions & orders grid (Trade groups tab additions only).

**Components:** CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-106 ProfileBadge, CMP-124 TradeGroupSummaryCard, CMP-123 FlattenAllButton, CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-229 ArmToggle, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-049 Table, CMP-041 Menu, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-107 OrderTicket (host), CMP-100/101/102/231.

**API:** `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups`, `GET /api/v1/trade-groups`, `GET /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/amend`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/cancel`.

**WS:** topic `trade_groups` (`TradeGroupUpdate`, 100 ms coalescing, filters `exchange_account_ids`/`status`, scope `orders:read` on granted accounts).

**DB:** `trade_groups`, `trade_group_legs`, `orders`, `executions`, `positions`, `system_events`, `audit_log`, plus new `unwind_plans` / `unwind_steps` tables for the restartable compensating unwind of `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.5.1.

**Architecture modules:** M4 (Bybit adapter `RestClient` — per-UID token bucket, `X-Bapi-Limit-*` feedback), M13 (accounts & profiles), M14 (OMS — `TradeGroupFanout`, `AccountRateBudget`, `UnwindResumer`).

## Out of scope
- Profile schema, sizing algorithm, allowed-symbol validation, server-side risk caps, trade-group *definition* CRUD → **E28**.
- Order state machine, `orderLinkId` idempotency, reconciliation loop, order/position blotters → **E29**.
- Single-account order ticket UI → **E30**; chart/DOM direct manipulation → **E31**.
- Bracket/scaled child-order construction and the native-SL enforcement engine itself → **E32**; emulated OCO/iceberg/TWAP/chase → **E33**.
- Kill-switch and risk-cap engines → **E39**. Journal aggregation of closed groups → **E41**.
- Live-environment enablement → R4 / **E44**. Android, a separate admin app, and non-USDT-perp instruments are out of scope for the whole plan.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One ticket, five accounts, five protected legs
  Given trade group "Core5" contains five ready demo accounts with distinct profiles
  When the owner submits a market buy on BTCUSDT with a bracket against the group
  Then five legs are created, each sized by its own profile and each carrying a native exchange-side stop-loss
  And all five share one trade_group_id, are acknowledged within 1.5 s p95, and each leg is audited individually

Scenario: Two of five legs fail
  Given fault injection rejects the submissions for accounts C and D
  When the fan-out wave quiesces
  Then the group is partially_open, C and D show the exchange reason code and message, and a critical alert fires
  And the owner is offered "retry failed legs" and "unwind successful legs", each idempotent and audited

Scenario: The rate budget is the binding constraint
  Given account B's entry bucket is exhausted and atomicity is best_effort
  When the group is submitted
  Then A, C, D and E are sent immediately, B is Deferred with a visible deadline, and no request is dropped silently
  And with atomicity all_or_none nothing is sent at all and the response names the starved account and its refill ETA

Scenario: Crash mid-unwind
  Given an all_or_none unwind plan is running across three accounts and the backend is killed
  When the backend restarts
  Then UnwindResumer resumes the persisted plan before the OMS accepts new orders, skipping steps already done
  And every residual position still carries its native stop-loss
```

## Technical notes / design
Normative sources, in force verbatim: `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.7 (rate budgeting), §8.8 (native SL), §9.1–§9.6 (group model, per-account profile, sizing, fan-out algorithm, failure policy, unwind, lifecycle) and `20-architecture.md` §4.3 (three-bucket split, pre-flight reservation, deferred drain, partial-failure matrix, metrics). Where the two documents name the same policy differently (`atomic` vs `all_or_none`, `PartiallyAdmitted` vs `partially_open`), the **OpenAPI enum in `22-api-openapi.yaml` wins** and E34-T03 reconciles the prose.

Module boundaries: M14 owns `TradeGroupFanout`, `AccountRateBudget` and `UnwindResumer`; M4's `RestClient` owns the token bucket's header feedback and the `10018` IP-wide back-off; M13 supplies frozen `profile_snapshot` values at fan-out time. Modules talk over the internal bus only (principle P7).

## Test plan
Per-ticket plans live on E34-Q01..Q06. Epic-level gates that must be green at the R3 PRR: the fan-out E2E suite (Playwright web + Electron), the k6 per-UID sustained-flow profile (1 h, 5 accounts, zero lost acks), the three chaos scenarios (WS kill mid-fan-out, backend restart mid-unwind, Postgres failover mid-fan-out), the axe + manual screen-reader pass on SCR-061/062, and the native-SL-escape suite's fan-out cases (zero escapes).

## Exit criteria
1. A single ticket targeting 5 demo accounts produces 5 correctly-sized orders under each account's own profile, each with a native SL, inside the per-UID budget, backend-added overhead ≤50 ms + ≤10 ms/account, group ack ≤1.5 s p95 (roadmap §7.3 #3, budget #4).
2. A fault-injection test failing 2 of 5 legs produces a visible reconciliation state, a correct one-click unwind, an audit trail and an alert (roadmap §7.3 #4).
3. No path in this epic can open a leg without a native SL; the invariant suite's fan-out cases show zero escapes (roadmap §7.3 #2).
4. k6 sustains order flow at the per-UID limit across 5 accounts for 1 h with zero lost acknowledgements and correct governor back-off; an injected `10018` produces an IP-wide back-off, never a silently dropped request.
5. Chaos: backend restart mid-fan-out and Postgres failover mid-unwind both resume to a correct, reconciled state with every residual position protected.
6. SCR-061/SCR-062 pass axe-core and a manual screen-reader pass; the partial-failure summary is announced via `role="alert"`.
7. STRIDE model finalized with all Critical/High closed; a Manager fanning out to an out-of-scope account receives 403, an audit row, and no adapter call is made.

## Risks
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| **R3 Real-time cost** — rate-limit exhaustion under fan-out | Three-bucket per-UID governor with a reserved `critical` slice; pre-flight reservation across all UIDs; K01 measures the real per-endpoint numbers before the governor is finalized. |
| **R11 Alert reliability** — a partial failure nobody sees | `partially_open` is a first-class state on the WS topic, the ticket, the manager and the risk dashboard; `unwind_incomplete_total ≥ 1` pages. |
| **R7 Data accuracy** — local fill accumulator vs exchange truth | Unwind and aggregation always read `GET /v5/position/list` as authoritative; qty drift is adopted, recorded and audited as `order.adopted_untracked`. |
| **R5 Scope** — the epic abuts E28/E29/E32/E33 | Explicit out-of-scope list above; consumed interfaces are named, never re-implemented. |
| **R10 Key-person** — one engineer owns the unwind state machine | §9.5.1 is fully normative in the plan; T03 keeps it in sync; pairing is mandatory on E34-S03. |

## Security notes
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 every ticket in this epic is treated as `security`-labelled: it touches `area/oms-execution` order placement and the fan-out safety invariant. Threats from `04-security-program.md` / STRIDE (E34-X01): **Spoofing** — a forged `arm_token` or replayed idempotency key re-submitting a group; **Tampering** — client-supplied per-leg sizing overriding server-resolved sizing; **Repudiation** — a fan-out without a per-leg audit row; **Information disclosure** — another user's account labels/balances leaking through the group response or the `trade_groups` WS topic; **Denial of service** — a fan-out loop exhausting the shared per-IP budget and starving protective traffic; **Elevation of privilege** — a Manager fanning out to an account outside `granted_accounts`. Controls: server-side resolution of every leg parameter, `x-rbac: {permissions:[orders:write], scope: granted_accounts}` enforced before any adapter call, required idempotency key, the reserved `critical` rate bucket, and an `audit_log` row per leg. Data classification: financial/execution data and account scope; API secrets are never handled here (they stay in the M2 vault) — only referenced by account id.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-061 and SCR-062 are real tables with textual row status; the partial-failure summary is `role="alert"`; the send button names the account count ("Send group (3 accounts)"); exclusion reasons are always text, never colour alone. WCAG 2.2 AA, with no "owner/admin surface" exception (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8).

## Performance notes
Budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2): backend-added fan-out overhead ≤50 ms + ≤10 ms/account, parallelized not serial. Preview ≤300 ms (SCR-061). Group ack ≤1.5 s p95 for 5 accounts (ADR-0008 validation gate S4). `oms_fanout_skew_seconds` p99 ≤1.5 s. SCR-062 grid stays under 4 ms scripting per frame with 50 open groups × 5 legs.

## Observability

Audit actions: `trade_group.submit`, `trade_group.unwound`, `positions.flatten`. `system_events` rows of kind `rate_limit` on every `10018`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike is Done (100% rollup) or explicitly descoped with a disposition recorded here.
- [ ] The seven epic-level exit criteria above are verified end to end, not merely per child.
- [ ] Coverage rolled up: ≥85% backend (OMS/risk modules ≥90%), ≥80% frontend; zero open P0/P1 bugs against E34's scope.

- [ ] security: STRIDE finalized, all Critical/High closed or Owner-accepted, Security engineer sign-off (E34-X03).
- [ ] QA sign-off: epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded (E34-Q06).

## Dependencies

title: UX research: how an owner reasons about a multi-account fan-out and its partial failure
body:
## Context
SCR-061 (trade-group ticket) and SCR-062 (trade-group manager) are the two screens E34 introduces. Both are new interaction territory: no prior screen in the product asks a user to reason about *N simultaneous executions with different sizes on different accounts*, and both have a failure state — a partially-executed fan-out — that `14-screens-catalogue.md` requires to be **"drawn as the primary design case, not an afterthought"**.

The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence) applies: no frontend work on E34-S04/S05 (Sprint 19) starts until the design tickets are Status=Done, and they must have been Done for ≥2 sprints.

Fan-out is the one place in the product where a single click commits capital on several accounts at once, and where "it half-worked" is an expected outcome rather than an incident. Before drawing anything we need to know how the owner and the account managers actually think about the group: as one trade, or as N trades that happen to be issued together? The answer decides whether SCR-061's primary object is the aggregate or the per-account row, and whether a partial failure reads as "the trade is damaged" or "three of my trades are fine and two need attention".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Semi-structured sessions with the Owner and the account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`), 45 min each, covering: mental model of the group, tolerance for asymmetry between accounts, what they would do first on a partial failure, and what "unwind" should mean to them.
- A concept test using the existing SCR-061 ASCII wireframe in `14-screens-catalogue.md` plus two alternative framings (aggregate-first vs per-account-first) — measure comprehension of "2 of 3 accepted" and of the three recovery actions.
- A decision test on recovery-action wording: **Retry failed** / **Unwind accepted** / **Leave as is** vs alternatives — the current catalogue copy says "Flatten accepted", and `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.5.1 calls the operation an *unwind*; the vocabulary must be settled here, once, and then used identically in UI, API errors, alerts and the journal.
- A findings deck plus a one-page "design principles for fan-out" note that D02/D03 are held against, and any resulting update to `10-personas.md` / `13-user-flows.md` F5.
- Explicit answer to four questions: (1) aggregate-first or per-account-first? (2) is per-row override an expected affordance or a trap? (3) how much rate-limit detail does the user want to see (a chip, a countdown, or nothing)? (4) should "close group 50%" mean 50% of each leg or 50% of the aggregate?

## Out of scope
- Any hi-fi visual work → D02/D03. Usability testing of built software → E34-Q06.
- Research on the single-account ticket (E30's research covers it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The four questions are answered with evidence
  Given at least three sessions with the Owner and manager personas
  When the findings are written up
  Then each of the four framing questions has a recommendation with the supporting observations cited

Scenario: Partial-failure comprehension is measured
  Given participants are shown a 2-of-3 partial failure
  Then the proportion who correctly state what happened and what each recovery action would do is recorded
  And any action whose meaning is misread by more than one participant is re-worded and re-tested before the research closes

Scenario: One vocabulary is chosen
  Then a single term for each recovery operation is recorded and adopted by D02, D03, the API error copy and the alert copy
```

## Technical notes / design
Recruit from the actual users (this is a private, single-owner product; the "user base" is the Owner plus a few managers, so n is small by construction — depth over sample size). Sessions recorded with consent; recordings stored in the team drive, not the repo.

## Test plan
N/A as software testing. Research quality bar: two researchers independently code the sessions and reconcile; findings that only one observed are marked as weak signal.

## Security notes
Sessions must not surface real API keys, account ids or balances — use the standard demo fixture data. Recordings contain the Owner's trading opinions and are treated as confidential; no recording leaves the team drive. Data classification: confidential, non-PII beyond participant identity.

## Accessibility notes
At least one session must include an assistive-technology scenario walkthrough (keyboard-only, screen reader) so the a11y constraints on SCR-061 are informed by intent, not retrofitted at D04.

## Performance notes
Findings must include the users' *tolerated* latency for the preview and for group ack — used to sanity-check the 300 ms / 1.5 s budgets from the user's side rather than only the engineering side.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts published in Figma, linked on this ticket, and the matching `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` entries updated to match.
- [ ] Every state from the screen-catalogue entry drawn: previewing, ready, partial-send in progress, partial failure, rate-limit backoff, blocked (account in lockout), empty, loading, error.
- [ ] The screen's "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `14-screens-catalogue.md` ticked item-by-item by the CDO or delegate, recorded as a comment.
- [ ] a11y annotations present: focus order, roles, live-region usage, contrast tokens, ≥24 px hit targets, text equivalents for every colour-coded state.
- [ ] Status=Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming FE story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence).
- [ ] Handoff walkthrough held with the implementing FE engineer and recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] Design tokens used are existing `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens, or a design-system contribution ticket is filed for any new one.

- [ ] Findings deck linked from both D02 and D03 and referenced in their design rationale.
- [ ] Vocabulary decision recorded and adopted by the API error copy (a comment on E34-S03).

## Dependencies

`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §13 lists two open spikes this epic depends on: **S7 Rate-limit truth** ("actual `X-Bapi-Limit` behaviour per endpoint group on a real UID → documented per-group budgets") and **S4 Multi-account fan-out** ("latency and rate budget with 3–5 sub-accounts on demo → all legs < 1.5 s, no 10018 under the designed budget"). Both are gates on ADR-0008's validation section.

The governor in E34-T02 hard-codes a bucket split (`critical` 40% / `entry` 40% / `poll` 20% of a default 10 req/s) and a set of refill rates taken from documentation that `21-database-schema.md` §Risk table row 3 explicitly flags as *"sourced from a mirror, not primary docs"*. Building the governor on unverified numbers would make every downstream latency and back-off assumption unfalsifiable. This spike replaces the assumptions with measurements before T02 finalizes its defaults.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A throwaway async harness under `spikes/e34-rate-limits/` driving the real Bybit **demo** endpoint `api-demo.bybit.com` with 3–5 demo sub-accounts registered through E27's vault (read keys through the normal vault API — never paste keys into the harness).
- Measure, per endpoint class of `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.7 (`order.create`, `order.amend`, `order.cancel`, `order.cancel_all`, `position.read`, `account.read`):
  - the observed `X-Bapi-Limit`, `X-Bapi-Limit-Status`, `X-Bapi-Limit-Reset-Timestamp` header values and their refill behaviour over a 60 s ramp;
  - whether the budget is genuinely shared across two keys of the same UID and genuinely independent across UIDs;
  - the retCode actually returned when the limit is crossed (`10006` per-UID vs `10018` per-IP) and the real recovery time for each;
  - the shared per-IP ceiling under 5 concurrent UIDs.
- Measure fan-out latency: one intent → 3 and 5 concurrent `POST /v5/order/create` calls with attached `stopLoss`, 30 repetitions, reporting p50/p95/p99 per-leg ack and whole-group ack, plus cross-leg skew.
- Record whether `stopLoss` attaches inline on `order/create` for linear perps (which sets `sl_cost = 0` in the pre-flight reservation of `20-architecture.md` §4.3) or requires a follow-up `POST /v5/position/trading-stop` (`sl_cost = 1`).
- Output: a comparison table + an ADR amendment to `27-adrs/ADR-0008-trade-group-fanout.md` §Validation recording the measured numbers, and follow-up tickets if a number invalidates a design rule.

## Out of scope
- Any production-shippable code. The harness is explicitly throwaway (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.1).

```gherkin
Scenario: Fan-out latency gate
  Given 5 demo accounts each submitting one entry with an attached stop-loss
  When 30 fan-out repetitions complete
  Then whole-group ack p95 is reported against the 1.5 s ADR-0008 gate
  And if p95 exceeds 1.5 s the spike files a follow-up ticket naming the dominant latency component before closing

Scenario: A measurement contradicts the design
  Given the measured per-UID order.create capacity differs from the assumed 10/s by more than 20%
  When the spike is written up
  Then the ADR is amended, E34-T02's default configuration values are updated on its ticket before it starts
  And 32-risk-register.md is updated with the revised R3 exposure
```

## Technical notes / design
Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. Decision criteria stated up front:
- If per-UID budgets prove *not* independent across UIDs, the whole three-bucket-per-account model in `20-architecture.md` §4.3 collapses into a single global governor — that is a P0 architecture change and E34-T02 is re-planned before it starts.
- If group ack p95 > 1.5 s at 5 accounts on demo, `max_concurrent_legs` and the submission ordering (descending notional, `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.4 rule 3) are retuned and the number is re-measured before T02 closes.
- If `stopLoss` cannot attach inline, `sl_cost = 1` becomes the default in the pre-flight reservation and every latency budget gains one round trip per leg.

Harness sketch: `asyncio.gather` over N signed clients, one per UID, with a shared `httpx.AsyncClient` so the per-IP ceiling is exercised realistically; every response's rate headers are appended to a Parquet file for analysis in DuckDB. Use only `reduce_only` / immediately-cancelled orders so no demo position is left open; assert flat at the end of each run.

## Test plan
Not a production ticket: no unit/coverage obligation. The deliverable's own validity is checked by (a) re-running the ramp twice and confirming the numbers reproduce within 10%, and (b) a second engineer re-reading the harness for a measurement bug (e.g. client-side queueing inflating observed latency).

Demo keys only, fetched through the E27 vault API — never written to the harness, a shell history, or the spike branch. The spike must not disable the withdrawal-permission self-check. Any raw response capture is scrubbed of `api_key` and signature headers before being committed. Data classification: no PII; demo financial data only. Security review label: yes (key handling).

This spike *is* the performance measurement. Reference budgets: `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2 budget #4 (≤50 ms backend-added + ≤10 ms/account) and ADR-0008's 1.5 s / 5-account gate.

title: Write the black-box test plan for trade-group fan-out
body:
## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` §SDLC requires a black-box QA test plan per feature, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes QA sign-off non-skippable for every Story. E34 has two properties that make a written plan indispensable rather than ceremonial: its most important behaviours (partial failure, rate-limit deferral, unwind) are **hard to produce by accident**, and its acceptance depends on *what did not happen* (no leg without a stop, no silent drop, no double close) as much as on what did.

This ticket writes the plan before the code exists, from the specification, so it tests the requirement rather than the implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box test plan document at `qa/plans/E34-trade-group-fanout.md` covering every story in the epic, organised as scenario → preconditions → steps → expected → evidence to capture.
- Coverage of, at minimum:
  - **Preview (E34-S01):** mixed-profile sizing, skip vs failure vs warn classification, below-minimum handling, stale-equity handling, out-of-scope account, side-effect-freeness.
  - **Execution (E34-S02):** 3- and 5-account success; per-profile sizing correctness checked against a hand-computed expectation; native SL present on every leg verified **at the exchange**, not in our UI; `all_or_none` pre-validation rejecting without sending; `best_effort` deferral; idempotent re-submit; arm-token and kill-switch refusal.
  - **Partial failure and unwind (E34-S03):** 2-of-5 rejection; retry-failed; unwind-accepted; unwind restart; fill-during-unwind; qty drift; deadline exceeded → incomplete with residual still protected; divergence badge within 30 s.
  - **Group actions:** close 50% with heterogeneous lot sizes; move stop across legs with different offsets; cancel working orders; per-leg result reporting.
  - **UI (E34-S04/S05):** every catalogue state; confirmation copy restating leg counts; Viewer/Manager/Owner RBAC rendering.
- **Environment and data plan**: which demo accounts, which profiles, which symbols, how to force each failure (fault-injection hooks, fixture names, feature flags), and how to return the environment to a flat, clean state after each run.
- **Exploratory charter set** (session-based, 90 min each) with explicit charters, e.g. "explore what happens when an account's key is revoked between preview and send", "explore rapid repeated sends of the same group", "explore browser tab close mid-fan-out".
- Traceability table mapping every plan scenario to a US id and to an acceptance criterion of the implementing ticket, so gaps are visible.

## Out of scope
- Executing the plan → E34-Q06 (and per-story QA sign-off). Automation → E34-Q02/Q03/Q04.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every Must story is covered
  Given US-PROF-006, US-PROF-007, US-PROF-008, US-ORD-010, US-ORD-013 and US-ORD-014
  When the traceability table is reviewed
  Then every scenario in those stories maps to at least one plan case, and every plan case maps back to a story or an acceptance criterion

Scenario: Failure states are reachable
  Given each negative scenario in the plan
  Then the plan names the concrete mechanism used to produce it (fault-injection hook, fixture, flag, or manual exchange action)
  And no scenario is documented as "observe if it happens"

Scenario: The environment returns to clean
  Then each case ends with a stated teardown that leaves all demo accounts flat with no working orders
```

## Technical notes / design
The "verify at the exchange, not in our UI" rule is the plan's backbone for the safety invariant: every SL assertion is made by querying Bybit demo directly (`GET /v5/position/list`, `GET /v5/order/realtime`), because a UI that believes a stop exists is exactly the failure mode we are guarding against.

## Test plan
Self-referential: the plan is reviewed by the Architect and a backend engineer for scenarios the spec implies but the plan misses; the review is recorded.

## Security notes
The plan includes the abuse cases from E34-X02 as black-box cases (out-of-scope account, tampered quantity, replayed idempotency key, forged arm token) so security behaviour is verified by QA as well as by the security track. Demo keys only; the plan must forbid using live keys anywhere.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes the keyboard-only and screen-reader walkthroughs for SCR-061/062 as black-box cases, using D04's screen-reader script as the expected result. The formal audit remains E34-Q05.

## Performance notes
The plan records where the budget assertions live (preview ≤300 ms, group ack ≤1.5 s p95) and that they are measured by E34-Q03 rather than by stopwatch during manual runs.

## Observability
Each case names the metric or audit row that should also confirm the outcome (e.g. `oms_fanout_deferred_total` for the deferral case, `trade_group.unwound` for the unwind case) — cross-checking behaviour against telemetry catches silent instrumentation gaps.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test assets committed under the repo's test tree and wired into CI where automatable.
- [ ] Execution evidence attached (run log, k6 summary, Playwright report, axe report, chaos run notes).
- [ ] Defects filed as Bug tickets with `priority/*`, linked to this ticket and to the offending Story.
- [ ] Coverage/quality-gate impact recorded; no existing gate weakened.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.

body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 names fan-out explicitly in the R3 E2E gate: "Playwright web + Electron covering ticket, chart trading, DOM trading, bracket, **fan-out**, rule creation in both editors, alert firing, journal capture". This ticket contributes the fan-out journeys, driven from E34-Q01's plan and running against a backend wired to recorded Bybit fixtures plus a fault-injection hook, so failures are deterministic rather than dependent on the exchange's mood.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `e2e/trading/fanout/`, each run in both the web and the Electron project configurations:
  1. **Happy path 3 accounts** — select group, preview shows three different sizes, send, all three accepted, group reaches `open`, every leg shows its native SL, positions grid reflects the group.
  2. **Partial failure 2 of 5** — fault injection rejects two legs; assert the `role="alert"` summary text, the three recovery actions, the audit rows and the alert.
  3. **Retry failed legs** — retry succeeds; assert a new idempotency key was used and no duplicate order exists on the successful legs.
  4. **Unwind accepted legs** — assert reduce-only closes only, per-account ordering (cancel before close), group ends `failed` with `unwind_incomplete=false`, and every account flat.
  5. **Rate-limit deferral** — governor forced into starvation for one account; assert the deferred row, its countdown, and the terminal rejection on deadline with no order sent.
  6. **all_or_none rejection** — assert nothing was sent at all and the response names the starved account.
  7. **Group lifecycle on SCR-062** — open → partial failure banner → retry → "close group 50%" with heterogeneous lot sizes → closed, with the confirmation restating the leg count.
  8. **Kill-switch refusal** — engage kill-switch, attempt a fan-out from the ticket, assert refusal and audit.
  9. **RBAC** — Manager sees only granted accounts in the selector and receives 404/403 appropriately for a foreign group; Viewer sees no mutating controls.
- A shared fixture/harness: a fault-injection API on the test backend (`/__test__/fail-leg`, `/__test__/starve-account`) available only when `CV_TEST_HOOKS=1`, plus a deterministic clock control for deadlines.
- Wire the suite into the CI pipeline as a required check for `area/oms-execution` changes, with trace/video artefacts on failure.
- Flake budget: any spec flaking more than 1 in 50 runs is quarantined with a Bug filed the same day — the suite's value is entirely in being believed.

## Out of scope
- Load/soak → E34-Q03. Chaos/infrastructure faults → E34-Q04. a11y audit → E34-Q05. Unit/integration tests belong to their implementing tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All nine journeys pass in both projects
  Given the web and Electron Playwright projects
  When the fan-out suite runs in CI
  Then all nine specs pass in both, with traces retained for any failure

Scenario: Deterministic failure injection
  Given the fault-injection hook is used to reject legs C and D
  When the partial-failure spec runs 50 times
  Then it produces the same outcome every time and the flake rate is zero

Scenario: Test hooks cannot exist in production
  Given a production build
  Then the fault-injection routes are absent and a test asserting their absence is part of the suite

Scenario: The suite proves the safety invariant end to end
  Given the happy-path and partial-failure specs
  Then each asserts, by querying the exchange stub directly, that every opened leg carries a native stop-loss
```

## Technical notes / design
- Selectors use role/name queries (the same semantics the a11y work guarantees), never CSS classes — this couples the suite to the accessible contract rather than to styling and makes a11y regressions fail the E2E suite too.
- WS-driven assertions wait on application state, not timeouts; the only real sleeps permitted are the explicit deadline tests, which use the controllable clock.
- Each spec is fully self-cleaning: teardown flattens every account and cancels every working order, asserted before the test reports success.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* test code; its own quality gate is: 50 consecutive green runs of the full suite before it becomes a required check, and a deliberate mutation (disable the native-SL attach) must turn the suite red — a suite that cannot detect the thing it exists for is not done.

## Security notes
Test hooks are the main risk introduced here: they are compiled out unless `CV_TEST_HOOKS=1`, never enabled in staging or production, covered by a CI assertion, and flagged in the threat model (E34-X01) as an accepted, controlled surface. Tests use demo keys from the vault fixture, never live keys.

## Accessibility notes
Because selectors are role/name-based, the suite implicitly asserts accessible names exist ("Send group (3 accounts)", "Flatten all 5 legs of group tg_0912"). The dedicated audit is E34-Q05.

## Performance notes
Suite wall-clock ≤12 min in CI with sharding, so it can be a required check without throttling the merge queue.

body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 sets the R3 load gate precisely: **"k6: sustained order flow at the per-UID limit across 5 accounts for 1 h with zero lost acknowledgements and correct governor back-off"**. `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2 budget #4 sets the latency target (≤50 ms backend-added + ≤10 ms/account) and §6 requires load tests to run against **recorded Bybit fixtures**, not live Bybit, so they are deterministic and consume no real rate budget.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6 scripts under `load/k6/fanout/`:
  - `fanout_sustained.js` — 1 h, 5 accounts, order flow held at the per-UID limit derived from E34-K01's measurements; asserts zero lost acknowledgements (every submitted leg reaches a terminal state), correct back-off behaviour, and no naked position at any sample point.
  - `fanout_burst.js` — bursts that deliberately exhaust the `entry` bucket, asserting deferral rather than loss, and asserting `critical` availability never drops below the reserve.
  - `fanout_latency.js` — budget #4 measurement: backend-added overhead per group at N = 1..5 accounts, reporting the fixed and per-account components separately so the "≤50 ms + ≤10 ms/account" shape is verified, not just the total.
  - `preview_load.js` — SCR-061's preview endpoint at realistic typing rates, asserting the ≤300 ms p95.
- A staging backend profile wired to recorded Bybit fixtures with a configurable synthetic exchange latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), so results are reproducible across runs and machines.
- Thresholds encoded as k6 `thresholds` (build fails on breach), not as eyeballed dashboards.
- A results record committed per run (date, commit, environment, numbers) so regressions are detectable across the train, plus a Grafana dashboard snapshot.
- CI wiring: the latency and preview profiles run on every `area/oms-execution` PR (short duration); the 1 h sustained profile runs nightly and before the R3 PRR.

## Out of scope
- Chaos/fault-injection → E34-Q04. Functional correctness → E34-Q02. Frontend rendering performance → E34-S05's own budget checks.
- Live-environment load — explicitly forbidden.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The R3 load gate
  Given 5 accounts driven at the per-UID limit for one hour
  When the run completes
  Then every submitted leg reached a terminal state with zero lost acknowledgements
  And the governor's back-off behaviour matches the expected token accounting within 5%

Scenario: Budget #4 shape is verified
  Given latency runs at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 accounts
  Then the fitted fixed cost is ≤50 ms and the marginal per-account cost is ≤10 ms
  And a regression beyond 10% of either component fails the threshold

Scenario: Starvation defers, never drops
  Given a burst that exhausts the entry bucket on two accounts
  Then those legs are deferred and then either sent or rejected with RATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
  And no leg ends in an unknown state and critical bucket availability never falls below the reserve

Scenario: Preview holds its budget under typing load
  Given preview requests at 4 per second per user across 3 concurrent users
  Then p95 latency stays ≤300 ms
```

## Technical notes / design
- The synthetic exchange must model **per-UID independence and per-IP sharing**, otherwise the test cannot exercise the interesting contention. Its parameters come from E34-K01.
- "Zero lost acknowledgements" is asserted by reconciling the script's submitted set against the backend's terminal set at the end of the run — not by trusting HTTP responses.
- Run the sustained profile at least once against **demo** (not fixtures) before the PRR, at a deliberately reduced rate, to confirm the fixture model has not drifted from reality; record both numbers.

## Test plan
The scripts are themselves validated by a negative control: artificially lower a bucket's capacity and confirm the thresholds fail, proving the assertions can detect a regression.

## Security notes
Load tests never run against live and never use live keys (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §6 rationale: avoid consuming real rate budget and risking account state). The synthetic exchange must not be reachable from staging's normal routing. Any captured payloads are scrubbed of signatures and key ids.

This ticket *is* the performance verification for the epic: budget #4, the 1.5 s group-ack gate from ADR-0008, `oms_fanout_skew_seconds` p99 ≤1.5 s, and the ≤300 ms preview.

title: Run chaos scenarios against in-flight fan-outs and unwinds
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 sets the R3 chaos gate: **"WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out — all resume to a correct, reconciled state"**, and `24-internal-schemas.md` §17 lists the unwind's specific obligations including a "restart-mid-unwind resume test". E34 owns the fan-out and unwind halves of that gate.

The epic's whole safety argument rests on claims that are only true if tested destructively: that a crash mid-fan-out cannot double-place, that a crash mid-unwind cannot double-close, and that a residual position always keeps its native stop.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chaos scenarios under `chaos/e34/`, automated and repeatable, each asserting a *reconciled end state* rather than the absence of an error:
  1. **Backend kill immediately after the first leg's ack** (ADR-0008's own validation scenario) — on restart, reconciliation finds the leg, its native SL exists, and the group is `partially_open`.
  2. **Backend restart mid-fan-out** with legs in mixed states, including one leg whose `place_order` was in flight — assert the in-flight leg is resolved by `order_link_id` lookup, never blind-retried, and no duplicate order exists.
  3. **Backend restart mid-unwind** — `UnwindResumer` resumes the persisted plan before the OMS accepts new orders; steps already `done` are skipped; identical `order_link_id`s are re-sent; no position is closed twice.
  4. **Postgres failover mid-fan-out** and **mid-unwind** — assert no lost group/leg rows, no orphan legs, and that a plan interrupted between step transitions resumes from the last committed step.
  5. **Private WS kill for 60 s mid-group** — group state goes `unknown` for the affected account rather than optimistic, reconciliation restores truth on reconnect, and the UI shows "state unknown for sub_00N".
  6. **Injected `10018` during a fan-out wave** — IP-wide back-off engages, protective traffic still flows, and no request is dropped without a terminal status.
  7. **Key revoked mid-unwind** — the step fails permanently, a critical alert names the account, and the residual position retains its native SL.
  8. **Clock skew (`10002`) during submission** — requests are rejected and retried after correction; no leg is left `Unknown` without resolution.
- A chaos harness with deterministic injection points (process kill at a named await boundary, DB failover trigger, WS server kill) so scenarios are reproducible rather than opportunistic.
- Each scenario asserts the invariant set: **no naked position, no duplicate order, no double close, no orphan row, no unresolved Unknown**, plus the expected audit rows and alerts.
- Results recorded per run; the suite runs nightly against staging and is a PRR gate item for R3.

## Out of scope
- Chaos for emulated algos (TWAP restart) → E33; for replay/recording → E26; general infrastructure failover → E45 (this ticket contributes its fan-out scenarios to that epic's wider programme).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Kill after first ack
  Given a five-account fan-out and the backend is killed immediately after the first leg's acknowledgement
  When the backend restarts
  Then reconciliation finds that leg, confirms its native stop-loss exists at the exchange, and sets the group to partially_open
  And no duplicate order exists for that leg

Scenario: Restart mid-unwind does not double-close
  Given an unwind plan with close_position sent for account A and unacknowledged
  When the backend is killed and restarted
  Then the same order_link_id is re-sent, the exchange de-duplicates or the lookup resolves it
  And account A's position is closed exactly once

Scenario: Postgres failover loses nothing
  Given a failover during the submission wave
  Then every leg row is present with a consistent status, no orphan legs exist
  And the group's derived status matches the exchange's actual state after reconciliation

Scenario: Every scenario ends protected
  Given any chaos scenario that leaves a residual position

```

Injection points are named constants in the production code paths guarded by `CV_CHAOS_HOOKS` (off by default, absent from production builds), because "kill it at a random moment" is not reproducible and reproducibility is the entire value here.

Each scenario is run 20 times; a scenario that passes 19 of 20 is treated as failing, because the failure mode it guards against is precisely the rare interleaving.

Chaos hooks are a deliberate production-code surface and are threat-modelled in E34-X01 alongside the E2E test hooks: compiled out of production, asserted absent by a CI test, never enabled on any environment reachable from outside Tailscale. Demo accounts only.

Scenario 5 asserts the UI's degraded copy ("state unknown for sub_002") is rendered and announced — a chaos test doubles as an a11y assertion for the degraded state that is otherwise nearly impossible to reach.

## Performance notes
Recovery-time assertions: reconciliation completes within 10 s of restart for 5 accounts; `UnwindResumer` starts before the OMS opens for new orders (ordering assertion, not a latency one).

## Observability
Each scenario asserts its expected `system_events` rows, alerts (`unwind_incomplete_total`, `naked_position_alert_total`) and audit entries. A scenario that produces the right end state with no telemetry is a failure — silent correctness is unverifiable in production.

body:
## Context

title: Dry-run a fan-out and return resolved per-account sizing, risk and rejections
body:
## Context
`24-internal-schemas.md` §9.4 rule 1 is binding: **"Dry-run preview is mandatory in the UI before a multi-account submit. The preview is the same code path as execution (`dry_run=True`), so what is previewed is what is sent."** SCR-061's entire top half is that preview — a row per account showing the resolved qty, leverage, SL, risk and the reason for every exclusion.

This story implements `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` (`22-api-openapi.yaml`: "Runs the full fan-out pipeline without submitting anything, returning exactly what each leg would" do). It delivers the server half of **US-PROF-006** scenario 1 and **US-ORD-014** scenario 2 (group preview aggregates across accounts and expands per account), and it is the surface on which US-PROF-008's per-leg overrides are validated before anyone can send them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` handler per `22-api-openapi.yaml` — same request schema as `POST /trade-groups`, response mirroring the resolved leg shape, `x-rbac: {permissions:[orders:write], scope: granted_accounts}` (preview is write-scoped because it discloses per-account equity-derived sizing).
- `TradeGroupFanout.resolve(cmd, dry_run=True)` in M14 — one function, two callers (this endpoint and E34-S02), so preview/execute divergence is structurally impossible.
- Per-leg resolution pipeline in the order mandated by `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`account profile → request-level defaults → legs[].overrides`, later wins) calling into E28's sizing (`24-internal-schemas.md` §9.3) and E32's SL/TP derivation; each leg's wallet snapshot must be ≤2 s old or is refreshed first (§9.4 rule 2).
- Per-leg outcome classification, kept strictly distinct per §9.5 "Skips vs failures": **skip** (`symbol_not_allowed`, `below_min_notional`, `profile_disabled`, account key self-check failed) vs **failure** (`risk_limit_breached`, `INSUFFICIENT_MARGIN`) vs **warn** (within 12% of the daily-loss cap — the SCR-061 WARN row).
- `sizing_explanation` string per leg, human-readable and exactly as exemplified in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`"risk_based: 250 USD / (63100.00 - 62900.00) = 1.25 BTC capped by max_notional_usd 25000 -> 0.396 BTC"`).
- Group totals: total qty, total notional, estimated fee, aggregate risk in USDT and R (US-ORD-014).
- **Rate-budget visibility**: the preview reports, per account, whether the pre-flight reservation would succeed now and the refill ETA if not, without consuming tokens.
- Native-SL precondition check: a leg whose resolved parameters would produce no stop is marked rejected at preview time with `no_native_sl_possible` — it can never reach submission (`24-internal-schemas.md` §9.4 rule 5).
- Audit: `trade_group.preview` is **not** written to `audit_log` (it is not a state change) but is counted as a metric; an `arm_token` is *not* required for preview.

## Out of scope
- Actually sending anything → E34-S02. The endpoint must be provably side-effect-free apart from a possible wallet refresh.
- The sizing algorithm and risk caps themselves → E28.
- The SCR-061 UI → E34-S04.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Three accounts, three different sizes
  Given accounts Main (risk 0.5% equity), sub_001 (fixed 0.1 BTC) and sub_002 (risk 0.5% equity)
  When I preview a limit buy of BTCUSDT at 64010 with SL 63900 against the group
  Then each row returns its own resolved qty, leverage and SL price with a sizing_explanation
  And the group totals report total qty, notional, estimated fee and aggregate risk in USDT and R

Scenario: Excluded account states its reason
  Given sub_003's profile does not allow BTCUSDT
  When I preview the same intent
  Then sub_003 is returned as skipped with reason symbol_not_allowed and no resolved sizing
  And the skip is presented as a skip, never counted as a failure in the totals

Scenario: Below minimum lot
  Given sub_004's resolved quantity is 0.0004 BTC and the symbol minimum is 0.001
  Then sub_004 is skipped with below_min_notional naming the minimum
  And the response includes the minimum so the UI can offer it as a one-click choice

Scenario: Preview never sends
  Given a preview request for five accounts
  When it completes
  Then zero calls were made to POST /v5/order/create and zero rate-budget tokens were committed
  And no trade_groups or trade_group_legs row was created

Scenario: A leg that cannot carry a stop is rejected in preview
  Given a leg whose profile defines no SL offset and the request supplies none
  Then that leg is rejected with no_native_sl_possible and the group is flagged not-submittable as configured

Scenario: Out-of-scope account
  Given a Manager whose granted_accounts exclude account C
  When the preview request names account C as a leg
  Then the response is 403, no sizing for C is computed or returned, and an audit row records the attempt
```

## Technical notes / design
- `resolve()` returns `ResolvedFanout(legs=[ResolvedLeg...], totals=..., admission=[AccountAdmission...])`. `ResolvedLeg` carries `status ∈ {ok, warn, skipped, rejected}`, `resolved` (qty, leverage, sl_price, tp_price, notional_usd, risk_usd, sizing_explanation) or `None`, and `error`/`skipped_reason`.
- Decimal discipline: every quantity is rounded **down** to `lotSizeFilter.qtyStep` and every price to `priceFilter.tickSize` from the instrument cache, using the quantization table of `24-internal-schemas.md` §1.5. Rounding direction is never "nearest" for size — an over-size is a risk breach.
- Wallet freshness: `equity` older than 2 s triggers a `poll`-bucket refresh; if the refresh fails the leg is returned `warn` with `stale_equity` and risk-based sizing is disabled for it (US-ORD-014 scenario 3).
- Idempotency: preview requires no idempotency key (no state change) — explicitly noted so the UI does not burn keys on every keystroke.
- Debounce contract for the UI: the endpoint must tolerate 5 calls/second/user; beyond that the gateway limiter returns 429 with `Retry-After` (E05's limiter, not the OMS governor).
- Error codes surfaced: `symbol_not_allowed`, `below_min_notional`, `profile_disabled`, `risk_limit_breached`, `stale_equity`, `no_native_sl_possible`, `rate_budget_would_exceed`.

## Test plan

- **Contract:** response validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml`'s preview schema in CI; the request schema is asserted to be *identical* to `CreateTradeGroupRequest` by a schema-equality test, so the two endpoints can never drift.
- **Side-effect test:** the whole preview path runs against a Bybit stub that fails the build if any order-mutating endpoint is called.
- **Integration:** recorded fixtures `fixtures/oms/preview_mixed_profiles.json` (3 ok, 1 skip, 1 warn) and `fixtures/instruments/btcusdt_filters.json`.
- **Perf:** preview p95 ≤300 ms for 5 accounts (SCR-061 budget) measured with warm wallet snapshots and once with a forced refresh.
- **E2E:** covered by E34-Q02.

## Security notes
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 every ticket in this epic is treated as `security`-labelled: it touches `area/oms-execution` order placement and the fan-out safety invariant. Threats from `04-security-program.md` / STRIDE (E34-X01): **Spoofing** — a forged `arm_token` or replayed idempotency key re-submitting a group; **Tampering** — client-supplied per-leg sizing overriding server-resolved sizing; **Repudiation** — a fan-out without a per-leg audit row; **Information disclosure** — another user's account labels/balances leaking through the group response or the `trade_groups` WS topic; **Denial of service** — a fan-out loop exhausting the shared per-IP budget and starving protective traffic; **Elevation of privilege** — a Manager fanning out to an account outside `granted_accounts`. Data classification: financial/execution data and account scope; API secrets are never handled here (they stay in the M2 vault) — only referenced by account id.

Ticket-specific: preview discloses **per-account equity-derived sizing**, which is a balance oracle. It is therefore `orders:write`-scoped, not `orders:read`, and an out-of-scope account id must be rejected before any sizing is computed (not filtered from the response afterwards).

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the endpoint. It is however the a11y *enabler* for SCR-061: every exclusion carries a text reason and every row a text status, so the UI never has to encode meaning in colour alone.

## Performance notes
Preview ≤300 ms p95 for 5 accounts (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-061). Wallet refreshes draw from the `poll` bucket only and never from `entry`/`critical`. The endpoint is read-only with respect to the rate governor: it may *inspect* availability but never `commit`.

## Observability

title: Execute a fan-out with admission control, parallel submission and a native SL per leg
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** Admission control stays in the per-UID rate-limit governor (MUSTNOT-02); this ticket drives the `B2`/`B3` charts for parallel submission and per-leg native SL, with no estimate change.

This is the core of **US-PROF-006**: "one submit creates per-account orders under each account's profile". It turns the resolved preview from E34-S01 into real orders through `POST /api/v1/trade-groups`, under the governor from E34-T02, with the safety invariant of `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.8 holding on every leg.

The sequencing is not negotiable and comes from `20-architecture.md` §4.3 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.4: **pre-flight reservation across all target UIDs first, placement second**. "Discovering exhaustion mid-loop would leave a group half-placed with no defined semantics" — so admission control precedes placement, and placement runs one `asyncio.Task` per account so a throttled account cannot head-of-line-block its siblings.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `POST /api/v1/trade-groups` handler per `22-api-openapi.yaml`: required idempotency key, `x-rbac: {permissions:[orders:write], scope: granted_accounts}`, `202 Accepted` returning the `TradeGroup` with per-leg resolved parameters and statuses.
- `TradeGroupFanout.execute(cmd)` in M14 implementing the §9.4 sequence diagram end to end: load profiles + wallets + instrument → size each leg (reusing E34-S01's `resolve()`) → RiskGate check → rate-budget pre-flight across all UIDs → persist group + legs with `status=submitting` → parallel submission → derive group status.
- **Atomicity modes** exactly as in the OpenAPI enum: `best_effort` (default — every leg attempted, failures reported per leg, group ends `partially_open`) and `all_or_none` (pre-validate every leg; abandon without sending anything if any fails validation; a post-send failure triggers the compensating unwind of E34-S03). The prose alias `abort_on_first` from `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.5 is supported as a rule-originated policy.
- **Pre-flight reservation** via E34-T02: `reserve(entry, cost=1 + sl_cost)` per account held for `CV_FANOUT_RESERVATION_TTL_MS`; `atomic` releases all and rejects with `RATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` naming the starved accounts and their refill ETA; `best_effort` sends the admitted accounts and marks the starved ones `Deferred` with `CV_FANOUT_DEFER_DEADLINE_MS`.
- **Bounded parallel placement**: `max_concurrent_legs` (default 5, from the request), one task per account, legs started in **descending leg notional** (§9.4 rule 3) so the largest, most consequential leg goes first.
- **Native SL on every leg**: the entry is submitted with `stopLoss` attached where the adapter's `supports_attached_sl_tp` capability allows; otherwise `POST /v5/position/trading-stop` is issued on first fill within a 2 s deadline (§8.8 rules 1–2). `native_sl_confirmed` / `native_sl_confirmed_at` are written on the leg. A leg that cannot attach one is aborted rather than opened naked (§9.4 rule 5).
- **Deferred drain**: per-account FIFO; on deadline expiry the child goes `Deferred → Rejected(RATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED)`, never `Unknown`.
- Deterministic `orderLinkId` per child from the `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3 generator (its `group22` segment is the trade-group UUID), allocated once before the first send, so a retry or restart re-sends an identical id and Bybit de-duplicates.
- Kill-switch and risk-cap gating: the fan-out consults E39's validator **before** any adapter call; an engaged kill-switch rejects with `trading_disabled` and nothing is sent.
- `arm_token` validation (US-ORD-005) — a group submit without a valid arm token is rejected when the confirmation policy requires arming.
- Audit: one `trade_group.submit` row for the group plus one `orders.submit` row per leg (`21-database-schema.md` audited-action vocabulary), all written before the network call.
- Drive the fan-out's parallel submission and per-leg native-SL confirmation through the `B2` (`trade_group`) root chart and its invoked `B3` (`leg`) children built by `statechart.factory.build(...)`. Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b02_trade_group.py` / `b03_leg.py` as `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`; services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b02_trade_group.py` / `test_b03_leg.py` membership for the states this story introduces.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.


## Out of scope
- Partial-failure UX, the unwind state machine and per-leg retry → **E34-S03**.
- The governor's internals → E34-T02. Sizing/risk-cap logic → E28. Bracket child construction and the SL enforcement engine → E32. Emulated algos (`algo.kind` other than `none`/`scaled`) → E33 (the request field is accepted and routed, the strategies are E33's).
- Any UI → E34-S04.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fan-out to three accounts
  Given group Core3 is selected and I submit a market buy with a bracket
  When the group is accepted
  Then three per-account orders are created, each sized and levered by its own profile, each with a native exchange-side stop-loss
  And all three are linked under one trade_group_id and each leg is audited individually

Scenario: Admission control precedes placement
  Given account B cannot reserve its entry tokens within CV_FANOUT_ADMIT_WAIT_MS and atomicity is all_or_none
  When the group is submitted
  Then zero orders are sent, all reservations are released, and the response is RATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED naming account B and its refill ETA

Scenario: Best-effort deferral is never silent
  Given the same starvation with atomicity best_effort
  Then the other accounts are sent immediately, account B's leg is Deferred with a visible deadline
  And on deadline expiry that leg becomes Rejected with RATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, never Unknown, because nothing was sent

Scenario: A slow account cannot block its siblings
  Given account A's submission takes 1200 ms and accounts B and C take 90 ms
  When the fan-out runs
  Then B and C are acknowledged without waiting for A, and oms_fanout_skew_seconds records the spread

Scenario: No leg is ever opened naked
  Given the adapter reports the stop attach failed for account C after the entry was accepted
  When the 2 s attach deadline passes with no exchange-side SL observed
  Then one retry runs immediately, and on second failure the leg is closed reduce-only and a critical NakedPositionAlert is raised
  And the attempt, the retry and the close are all audited

Scenario: Kill-switch beats everything
  Given the kill-switch is engaged
  When a fan-out is submitted by any path including the rule engine
  Then it is rejected with trading_disabled before any adapter call and the rejection is audited

Scenario: Idempotent re-submit
  Given a fan-out request is retried with the same idempotency key after a client timeout
  Then the original trade group is returned unchanged and no second set of orders is created
```

## Technical notes / design
- The submission wave is `asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)` over one task per account, bounded by a `Semaphore(max_concurrent_legs)`; per-leg exceptions become leg errors, never a 500 for the group.
- Group status is **derived**, never assigned (E34-T01's `TradeGroupLifecycle`), so a race between a WS fill and a REST ack cannot produce an inconsistent group.
- REST ack is **acceptance only**; the WS execution/order stream is the source of truth (E29/ADR-0006). A leg is `open` when the private stream says so, not when the REST call returns.
- Unknown handling (ADR-0006): a leg whose `place_order` times out after sending goes to `Unknown` and is resolved by `order_link_id` lookup (`GET /v5/order/realtime` then `/v5/order/history`), never by blind retry — "the system never silently retries a leg that might have executed" (ADR-0008 rule 5).
- `profile_snapshot` is frozen onto the leg at fan-out time (ADR-0008 rule 3) so a later profile edit cannot rewrite the history of an executed trade.
- Error codes: `RATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `trading_disabled`, `risk_limit_breached`, `symbol_not_allowed`, `no_native_sl_possible`, `arm_token_invalid`, plus the Bybit-mapped taxonomy of `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.6.
- Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B2.1-.8 / §B3.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2. Admission control and per-UID budgeting stay plain code (MUSTNOT-02).


## Test plan
- **Unit (≥90%):** admission-control decision table (atomic/best_effort × starved/not, per account); descending-notional ordering; deferred-queue transitions; `orderLinkId` determinism; arm-token and kill-switch gates; Unknown-resolution path.
- **Contract:** request/response against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; emitted `trade_groups` frames against the WS schema.
- **Integration (recorded Bybit fixtures):** 5-leg success; 2-of-5 rejection; a `10018` mid-wave; a WS disconnect between ack and fill; clock skew (`10002`); duplicate `orderLinkId`.
- **Safety suite (required check):** the fan-out entries of the native-SL-escape suite — attempt to open a position without a native SL through this endpoint by every parameter combination; **zero escapes** (roadmap §7.3 #2). A failure blocks merge, not just release (§7.4 Safety gate).
- **Perf:** budget #4 — backend-added overhead ≤50 ms + ≤10 ms/account measured with the exchange stubbed at a fixed latency; group ack ≤1.5 s p95 for 5 accounts on demo.
- **Load/chaos:** delegated to E34-Q03/Q04.
- **Fixtures:** `fixtures/oms/fanout_5legs_ok.json`, `fixtures/oms/fanout_2of5_rejected.json`, `fixtures/bybit/ret_10018.json`.
- pure-API unit tests of the b02/b03 binding modules with a `SimulatedClock`
- contract-suite membership covering the parallel-submission and per-leg-SL invariants


## Security notes
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 every ticket in this epic is treated as `security`-labelled: it touches `area/oms-execution` order placement and the fan-out safety invariant. Threats from `04-security-program.md` / STRIDE (E34-X01): **Spoofing** — a forged `arm_token` or replayed idempotency key re-submitting a group; **Tampering** — client-supplied per-leg sizing overriding server-resolved sizing; **Repudiation** — a fan-out without a per-leg audit row; **Information disclosure** — another user's account labels/balances leaking through the group response or the `trade_groups` WS topic; **Denial of service** — a fan-out loop exhausting the shared per-IP budget and starving protective traffic; **Elevation of privilege** — a Manager fanning out to an account outside `granted_accounts`. Controls: server-side resolution of every leg parameter, `x-rbac: {permissions:[orders:write], scope: granted_accounts}` enforced before any adapter call, required idempotency key, the reserved `critical` rate bucket, and an `audit_log` row per leg. Data classification: financial/execution data and account scope; API secrets are never handled here (they stay in the M2 vault) — only referenced by account id.

Ticket-specific: this is the highest-value target in the product — an endpoint that spends real money across N accounts. Required controls verified here: server-side resolution of every leg parameter (a tampered client cannot oversize — US-PROF-002 NFR), mandatory idempotency key, `granted_accounts` scope check before any adapter call, arm-token check, kill-switch check, and one audit row per leg written *before* the network call so a crash cannot lose the record of an attempt. Threat model E34-X01 must be Done before this story starts.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. Response fields (`status`, `error.message`, `sizing_explanation`, deferral deadline) are designed to be rendered as text by SCR-061.

## Performance notes
Budget #4: ≤50 ms backend-added + ≤10 ms/account, parallelized. ADR-0008 validation gate: all legs submitted within 1.5 s for 5 accounts. `oms_fanout_skew_seconds` p99 ≤1.5 s. Placement must not hold the DB transaction open across the network calls — persist `submitting`, commit, then send.

## Observability
`oms_fanout_total{atomicity,outcome}`, `oms_fanout_legs_total{status}`, `oms_fanout_duration_ms`, `oms_fanout_skew_seconds`, `oms_fanout_deferred_total{account}`, `oms_fanout_rejected_total{reason}`, `naked_position_alert_total`. Trace: one span per group with a child span per leg, carrying `trade_group_id` and `order_link_id`. Audit `trade_group.submit`, `orders.submit`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every acceptance-criteria scenario is verified by an automated test that names the scenario.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on touched backend packages; OMS/risk modules held to ≥90% by R3 local policy (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4).
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md` updated if the shipped contract diverged; contract tests green.
